body:
*Built 2026-11-20. Teaches how to read financial statements the way a forensic analyst does. Every worked example uses a real filing or a real data aggregator page, cited at the end of each lesson.*

**How to use this.** Do one lesson per sitting. Work each example yourself before you read the answer. The exercises use the same real numbers. Answers are at the end of each lesson.

**What this course adds to memdb.** It builds on records that already exist and does not repeat them:
- `insight:forensic-redflag-checklist` is the 18-flag checklist distilled from about 30 blow-ups.
- `insight:ind-as-accounting-levers` lists where reported profit and owner earnings diverge under Ind AS.
- `insight:beneish-m-score`, `insight:altman-z-score` and `insight:piotroski-f-score` give the definitions and cut-offs.
- `strategy:read-10k-efficiently` and `strategy:us-forensic-screen-workflow` cover the US filing workflow.

This course adds the mechanics: how to compute each test, which thresholds to use, worked numbers from real companies, and exercises.

**Data conventions**
- Indian figures are in ₹ crore, consolidated, from Screener.in (pages read 2026-11-20). Screener is a single aggregator, so every Indian number is **single-source** until you tie it to the annual report.
- US and IFRS figures come from SEC XBRL companyfacts (`tools/sec_fetch.py`), and each one carries its accession number. Those are primary filings.
- Screener folds exceptional items into "Other Income". Its "Free Cash Flow" is CFO minus capex, with no deduction for lease payments. Both conventions matter in the lessons below.
- This is research and self-education, not SEBI-registered advice.

**The one idea behind everything.** Profit is an opinion and cash is a fact, though cash can be managed too. Each technique below asks one of three questions:
1. Did the accrual turn into cash?
2. Was a cost moved somewhere you are not looking, such as the balance sheet, the CFF section, a subsidiary or a footnote?
3. Will this number recur?

data.section: Accounting forensics: a practical course (India + US)

title: course › Accounting forensics: a practical course (India + US)

body:
- **Samayat Services LLP, the PE promoter vehicle, is also VMM's transporter and warehouse operator** `[UDRHP risk factor 16]`, `[AR26 n.35]`.

| | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Transport paid to Samayat (₹ mn) | 142.9 | 223.1 | 255.9 | **721.0** |
| As % of total transport | 13.8% | 15.9% | 16.2% | **28.1%** [EST: 721/2,563] |
| Warehousing paid to Samayat (₹ mn) | 106.9 | 119.8 | 163.7 | **311.7** |
| As % of rent and warehousing | 61.9% | 59.7% | 54.9% | 46.6% |

  Q1 FY25 transport share was 22.3%. Rishay Services LLP (admin and facility management) and Rishanth Services LLP (quality control) also bill VMM: ₹7.3 cr in FY26.
- About ₹103 cr a year flows to the controlling shareholder's entity. That is about 8% of pre-Ind AS EBITDA, and the transport share has doubled since FY22.
- **Benign version:** a legacy logistics arm carved out at the 2018 buyout, priced at arm's length (the audit committee approves RPTs, and the auditor gave no qualification).
- **Malign version:** a margin-extraction channel that survives the PE exit or is sold with it.
- **Open questions:** (1) What happens to these contracts when Samayat's stake drops below 20%? (2) Rates per km and per sq ft against VMM's non-related transporters, which the RHP says are hired "on a needs basis" without agreements. (3) Who owns Samayat's trucks and warehouses? Use MCA filings of Samayat Services LLP. **Grade: soft flag, open** (not a hard disqualifier; there is no sign of diversion).

body:
- **Dealers:** 21 dealers, 120+ branches `[WEB: cummins.com]`. Distribution revenue ₹3,278 cr ÷ 21 ≈ **₹156 cr per dealer a year** [EST]; this flows through CIL's books, and the dealer's own revenue and margin are not disclosed. "Commission on sales" ₹30.9 cr (FY25 ₹21.0 cr, +47%) `[AR26 n.31]`. "Royalty income from dealers" is inside "other operating revenue – others" (₹134.9 cr) `[AR26 n.26]`. **The dealer pays CIL a royalty**, and CIL pays CMI one.
- **CIL sold its own distribution subsidiary,** Cummins Sales and Service Pvt Ltd (gain ₹44.15 cr, FY26) `[AR26 n.46]`. *Open: to whom, and at what price?*
- **LHP channel push:** 14 specialised "2S" dealers onboarded for low-kVA gensets `[AR26 MD&A]`. This is a test of whether CIL can win the price-sensitive band against KOEL and Mahindra.
- **GOEM economics:** not disclosed anywhere. The GOEM buys the engine, adds an alternator (often from **Cummins Generator Technologies India, CIL's associate**, which paid CIL a ₹117 cr dividend in FY26) plus canopy and panel, and sells to the end customer. **Part of the "alternator price hike" analysts blame for genset inflation `[CC-Q2FY27]` flows back to CIL as associate profit.** That is a small hidden hedge.
